'''Patricia Lynn Hersh''' (born 1973)<ref>Birth year from [http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2016004555.html Library of Congress catalog data], retrieved 2018-11-28.</ref> is an American mathematician who works as a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Oregon]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.uoregon.edu/profile/plhersh|title=Patricia Hersh {{!}} Department of Mathematics|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-29}}</ref> Her research concerns [[algebraic combinatorics]], [[topological combinatorics]], and the connections between combinatorics and other fields of mathematics.<ref name="michler"/>

==Education and career==
Hersh graduated ''magna cum laude'' with an A.B. in mathematics and computer science from [[Harvard University]] in 1995,<ref name="cv">{{citation|title=Curriculum vitae: Patricia L. Hersh|url=http://www4.ncsu.edu/~plhersh/cv-hersh.pdf|access-date=29 April 2020}}.</ref> with a senior thesis supervised by [[Persi Diaconis]].<ref name="michler"/> 
She completed her Ph.D. in 1999 at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], under the supervision of [[Richard P. Stanley]]; her dissertation was ''Decomposition and Enumeration in Partially Ordered Sets''.<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=37039}}</ref>

After postdoctoral positions at the [[University of Washington]], [[University of Michigan]], and [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]], she joined the faculty at [[Indiana University Bloomington]] in 2004,  moved to North Carolina State University in 2008, and then to the University of Oregon in 2019.<ref name="cv"/> She served as an [[American Mathematical Society]] Council member at large from 2011 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2010, Hersh won the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], funding a visiting position for her at [[Cornell University]].<ref name="michler">{{cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/ruth-i-michler-prize/michler-prize-2010-2011/|title=Ruth I. Michler Prize 2010–2011|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|access-date=21 January 2021}}.</ref> 
In 2015 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to algebraic and topological combinatorics, and for service to the mathematical community".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2015-11-17}}.</ref>
